codebook_exclusion: No architecture_mode, module_substrate, conflict_timing_geometry or conflict_spatial_geometry is recoded or opened; no human CODER_A/B identity used.

source_records.observation: Thrips feeding experiment used pollen of Actinidia deliciosa (and Echium plantagineum); reported 29–843 grains per thrips per day across treatments and extrapolated possible crop fitness costs. This was a laboratory feeding assay, not direct field confirmation of a new floral module.
Kiwifruit is dioecious, with male pollen-producing and female ovule-producing vines; pistil anatomy/pollen tube distribution tested in a separate study, not linked experimentally to thrips selection.

first_six.unresolved: No same-context genetic sex architecture comparison, natural pollen theft rate or matched male/female fitness; plant-wide sex segregation cannot be inferred as an evolved response to thrips feeding.

source_records.observation: A narrow passage between anther–stigma column and labellum forces Bombus haemorrhoidalis to touch anther and stigma during entry; Apis cerana collects pollen without stigmatic contact and is a pollen robber.

first_six.unresolved: Presence of functional filtering by a flower is not an assay of independent evolved module construction, same-trait pure functional optima, or architecture maintenance cost.

source_records.observation: Published original study compares hummingbird pollination with Trigona pollen theft and florivory; public summary reports most flowers visited by pollen collecting bees by mid-morning and substantial style damage. Exact primary paper anatomy/functional separation not retrieved.

first_six.unresolved: Primary full method/anatomy missing from reviewed source; do not code SHARED, SEPARATED or temporal-developmental modules.

source_records.observation: Staphylinid beetles removed pollen but did not deposit it onto stigmas; beetle abundance related to florets opening per day; bees visited more frequently than birds, yet bird-visited inflorescences had much higher fruit set. Evolutionary selection for bird-associated floret opening was proposed, not directly reconstructed.

first_six.unresolved: Opening florets across days is not proof of temporally programmed pollen dosing evolved to repel beetles; without time-aligned plant male fitness and alternatives no W_D-W_S.

source_records.observation: Inflorescences produce 10–35 newly opening flowers per day; nectar peaks at 04:00–06:00; bees primarily visit in the morning while hummingbirds contribute mostly afternoon visits; Trigona spinipes steals pollen/nectar early, frequently excluding hummingbirds. The temporal visitor pattern is observational, not a manipulated new pollen-release organ.

first_six.unresolved: Do not equate diel arrival order with pollen-source simultaneous-conflict classification, reversible cue plasticity, or permanently differentiated module.

source_records.observation: In a greenhouse experiment, removing pollen shortened the morphological male phase and depositing pollen shortened the morphological female phase. In a field survey, male and female functions saturated within hours, yet morphological sex phases persisted beyond functional saturation. The same species has stamens shedding pollen onto collecting hairs before anthesis; the stigma opens after hair retraction. This is a cue-responsive developmental schedule, NOT a reversible alternation back to an earlier floral phase or a demonstrated new module origin.

Low-efficiency halictid pollen visitors reduced siring success when effective Bombus visits were scarce, but not when effective pollinators were abundant; pollen colour affected visitor attraction. The fitness contrast and developmental mechanism come from different studies.

first_six.unresolved: Experimentally demonstrated phenological plasticity modifies the time spent in an existing developmental phase, but does not demonstrate an individually reversible sex-phase trajectory, a full reproductive fitness advantage over fixed timing, or evolved novelty induced by pollen thieves. The low-efficiency-bee siring evidence is from a separate 2004 study.
